title: Bhishma's fall
hook: the Kaurava commander loves the men he is fighting, and Duryodhana's friend Karna refuses to fight under him.

segments.voice: Yesterday the Bhishma Parva's Gita days ended with Yudhishthira walking unarmed to Bhishma, and Bhishma saying: ask me again another time. Did you offer someone respect before you disagreed? Day eight hundred twenty-five.

An army might want a commander who hates the enemy. Duryodhana's commander doesn't. When Duryodhana asked Bhishma to lead his forces, in the Udyoga book, the old man said yes, and then set terms. The sons of Pandu, he said, are as dear to me as you are. I will fight their armies for you. I will not kill them. And there was a second problem, standing right there in the hall: Karna. Today, Bhishma's fall begins, with the strange shape of the side he leads.
screen: `A COMMANDER WHO DOESN'T HATE` → `HIS TERMS: NOT THE FIVE BROTHERS` → `AND KARNA IN THE HALL`

segments.voice: Start with Karna. Bhishma and Karna don't get along. In the Udyoga book, when Bhishma ranks the warriors on his own side, he rates Karna low, and Karna is stung. So when Bhishma takes command, Karna makes a vow of his own. As long as Bhishma lives, Karna will not fight. When Bhishma falls, then he'll take the field against Arjuna. So the Kaurava side goes into battle with its commander holding back from the five brothers, and Karna sitting in his tent. Now add one more thing the epic told us long ago. When Bhishma was young, he gave up his claim to the throne and swore never to marry, so his father could marry again. In return, the epic says, his father gave him a gift: death would not take him until he chose it. Put those together and you have the riddle of the next days. Bhishma can't be beaten, and he won't be hurried. In the first day's fighting, the losses fall hard on the Pandava side. Uttara, the young prince of Virata, who held the reins for Arjuna in the cattle raid, is killed. So is his brother Shveta, at Bhishma's own hand. The family that sheltered the Pandavas pays first. So when we say Bhishma's fall, hold it as a question, not just an event. How do you bring down a man who loves you, who can't be beaten, and who decides for himself when he dies? The epic takes its time answering.
screen: `KARNA WON'T FIGHT WHILE BHISHMA LIVES` · `THE BOON: DEATH WHEN HE CHOOSES` · `VIRATA'S SONS FALL FIRST` · then, large: `HOW DO YOU BRING HIM DOWN?`

segments.voice: Sit comfortably. Let your breath come and go without managing it. Think of a commitment you carry, one that sometimes pulls against what you'd rather do. A job, a promise, a family role. Breathing in, feel its weight honestly. Breathing out, notice what in you still chooses to keep it. Don't decide anything. Just let both be true for a few breaths, the way Bhishma held two loyalties on the same field. If you pray, you can bring that commitment into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Bhishma's fall. Not yet. Today it's a riddle: a commander who loves the other side, and who will die only when he chooses.
Your line: Bhishma's fall. Today, notice one promise you keep even when it pulls against you, and name why you keep it. Day eight hundred twenty-five.

howItsDone: Bhishma's terms as commander, Karna's refusal to fight under him, and the boon that lets him choose his death are told in the Mahabharata's Udyoga, Adi and Bhishma books, and are familiar parts of retellings of the war.

accept, and promise to destroy them.

original.note: Bhishma, the grandsire, who swore never to marry or rule, and was given the gift of choosing his own death.

what a scholar hears: the boon from his father, given in the Adi book, shapes how the Bhishma book must end.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva (Sainya-niryana; Rathatiratha-sankhyana), Bhishma accepts command on terms; ranks Karna low; Karna's vow not to fight while Bhishma lives
Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Sambhava), Bhishma's vow and his father Shantanu's boon of death at will
Mahabharata, Bhishma Parva (Bhishma-vadha), the first day: Uttara slain by Shalya, Shveta slain by Bhishma

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Bhishma's terms on accepting command (the sons of Pandu dear to him; he will not slay them); Bhishma rating Karna an ardharatha (half-car warrior) and Karna's vow not to fight while Bhishma lives.
Confirm: Shantanu's boon that death would not come to Bhishma until he wished it (Adi Parva).

Confirm first-day deaths: Uttara (slain by Shalya) and Shveta (slain by Bhishma), both sons of Virata. The script says 'the losses fall hard on the Pandava side' on that day; check it matches Ganguli.
The script says Arjuna drove Uttara's chariot during the year in disguise (as Brihannala, in the cattle raid); confirm it matches how days 808–812 told it.
Audit (fresh pass): 'whose chariot Arjuna drove' reversed the cattle-raid roles taught on days 811-812 (Uttara held the reins while Arjuna fought); corrected.
